rationale: While early human clinical descriptions (such as the 18 pediatric patients characterized by Nashabat et al.) showed that skeletal myopathy and neurological features predominate without classic dilated cardiomyopathy, subsequent reports and experimental models directly conflict with the premise that SNUPN deficiency spares cardiac tissue. Specifically, Dai et al. (2026) documented a pediatric LGMDR29 patient presenting with isolated post-infectious acute myocardial injury and dramatically elevated CK/CK-MB, and Drosophila models of the SNUPN orthologue specifically display conduction defects and cardiomyopathy phenotypes. Additionally, major disease annotation resources (GeneCards, OMIM, MalaCards) associate SNUPN variation with cardiomyopathy phenotypes, refuting the claim that cardiac sparing reliably excludes SNUPN from cardiomyopathy-associated dystrophies.

evidence.text: Characterization of 18 children from 15 unrelated families with biallelic SNUPN variants identified an atypical limb-girdle muscular dystrophy with neurological defects, sarcolemmal splicing disruption, and cytoskeletal breakdown.

conflicts: Initial large cohort studies (Nashabat et al., 18 pediatric patients) showed that progressive structural cardiomyopathy was absent or not established as a primary core sign of SNUPN deficiency, whereas a subsequent pediatric report (Dai et al., 2026) showed acute isolated myocardial injury as the herald clinical manifestation.

Functional animal models (Drosophila SNUPN orthologue) manifest explicit cardiac conduction defects and cardiomyopathy phenotypes, conflicting with claims that SNUPN deficiency does not provoke intrinsic myocardial or conduction tissue vulnerability.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of adult and pediatric LGMDR29 patients display subclinical myocardial fibrosis by cardiac MRI or arrhythmogenic conduction changes under stress/infection?
new_directions.rationale: Echocardiography may miss early or focal myocardial tissue injury as seen in the acute post-viral myocarditis-like presentation of LGMDR29 reported by Dai et al.

new_directions.question_text: Does human SNUPN deficiency alter alternative splicing of cardiac-specific isoforms of titin (TTN), lamin A/C (LMNA), or dystrophin (DMD) in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes?
new_directions.rationale: Since SNUPN plays a central role in snRNP nuclear transport and spliceosomal dynamics, determining whether it disrupts cardiomyocyte-specific transcripts will explain why Drosophila models exhibit cardiomyopathy and conduction defects.
